chunks: And by this chain, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who is killed facing his oppression, he is a martyr.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Abu Maryam! Do you know what is 'facing his oppression'?' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! The man who is killed instead of his family, and instead of his wealth, and similar to that.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Abu Maryam! Indeed, from jurisprudence is the recognition of the truth.'
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of a martyr in Shia hadith regarding being killed against oppression?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi clarifies that martyrdom extends beyond battlefield death to include those killed defending their family, wealth, or self against oppression, a concept central to Shia jurisprudence. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes that 'knowing the truth' (irfan al-haqq) is an essential component of fiqh, linking legal status to deeper spiritual and epistemological recognition. This expands the traditional understanding of shahada to encompass civilian defense and personal integrity in the face of injustice.

en.hubeali: And by this chain, from Abu Maryam,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one being killed facing his attacker, so he is a martyr’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Abu Maryam! Do you know what is ‘facing oppression’?’ I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! The man who is killed instead of his family, and instead of his wealth and like that’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said:’ O Abu Maryam! It is from the jurisprudence, recognition of the truth’.
en.sarwar: 2. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from abu Maryam from Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, who has said the following:

“The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘If one is murdered over his stolen property he is a martyr.’ He (the Imam) then said, ‘O abu Maryam, do you know what is ‘murdered over his stolen property’? I replied, ‘I pray to Allah to keep me in the service of your cause, it is when a man is murdered defending his family, property and similar things.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is of fiqh (proper understanding) to know the truth.’”
